references.text: David says that all his days are written in God's book – God has full oversight of every detail of human life, just as Jesus assures that even the hairs on the head are numbered ([ref:Ps 139:16|Psalms 139:16]).
The preceding verse emphasizes God's care for the sparrows, which forms the basis for Jesus' argument that you are worth more than many sparrows ([ref:Lk 12:6|Luke 12:6]).

The context in which Jesus says 'Do not be afraid' – he has just explained that the disciples should not fear those who kill the body, but rather fear God who has power over all things ([ref:Lk 12:4-5|Luke 12:4-5]).

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus uses the same image that all the hairs on the head are numbered and that the disciples are worth more than many sparrows – 'Do not be afraid!' ([ref:Mt 10:30-31|Matthew 10:30-31]).

Saul swears that not a hair of Jonathan's head shall fall to the ground – an expression of God's protection down to the smallest detail, parallel to Jesus' words that the hairs are numbered ([ref:1 Sam 14:45|1 Samuel 14:45]).
The psalmist trusts that God has his tears in His bottle and has written them down – an expression of God's detailed care and oversight over human life ([ref:Ps 56:9|Psalms 56:9]).
Jesus later repeats the same promise to the disciples: 'But not a hair of your head shall perish' – an assurance of God's total care in the midst of persecution ([ref:Lk 21:18|Luke 21:18]).
Paul uses the same expression when he encourages his fellow travelers during the storm: 'Not a hair of anyone's head shall be lost' ([ref:Acts 27:34|Acts 27:34]).

The Lord says 'Do not be afraid' to Israel and assures them that He has redeemed them and called them by name – the same message of not fearing because God knows and values His people ([ref:Is 43:1|Isaiah 43:1]).

Jesus points to the birds under heaven whom God feeds, and asks 'Are you not worth much more than they?' – the same argument from the lesser to the greater regarding human value ([ref:Mt 6:26|Matthew 6:26]).
